name: core-recurrence
description: Recurrence on a table, D152 and #601: setRecurrence plans a row's occurrences of a calendar rule to the horizon in its zone, across a change of the clocks, a due date on a holiday of the row's calendar moved to the next business day; the open, remind, due, overdue and plan deadlines, each fire moving the occurrences on by its time and emitting opened, reminded, due and missed, in order, once each, a late fire catching up every one it passed; complete with what and who completed it, a repeat unchanged; skip, moveOne and listOccurrences; an afterDone recurrence dated from a missed due and from a late completion; a rule change that keeps the open occurrence; a relative recurrence read through its relation, planned when the horizon reaches it and dated again by setRecurrence with the rule it holds; the permissions and vetoes; and the define refusals. Cases written by hand in the recorded format, since no engine implements Recurrence. Each answer holds what the replayer compares: a record's id, data and behaviors, an operation's result, a refusal whole, in the core's words, and the events each step's commands wrote (events); what only the engine's store answers (sequence numbers, versions, timestamps, the document a define echoes) is left out.
